entities.name: Adalbert III of Saxony
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adalbert III of Saxony (c. 1010–1072) was a noble of the Saxon House of Ballenstedt whose career is connected to the early history of the Ascanian dynasty — the family that would produce the Margraves of Brandenburg and the Dukes of Saxony. The Ascanians' rise to prominence in the twelfth century was built on foundations laid in the eleventh century by figures like Adalbert III.

The Ballenstedt lineage occupied a significant position in Saxony's complex aristocratic landscape. Saxony was the most powerful duchy in the German kingdom — the land that had produced the Ottonian dynasty — and its internal aristocratic politics shaped imperial history throughout the eleventh century. The Ballenstedts/Ascanians gradually built up their territorial base in the area between the Harz Mountains and the Elbe.

Adalbert III's precise role in early Ascanian history is obscure due to limited primary sources for this early period of the family's history. His significance lies primarily in his position in the genealogical chain that led to the dynasty's great twelfth-century figures: Albert the Bear, who won the Margraviate of Brandenburg in 1157, and the Ascanians who shaped northeastern Germany for two centuries.
